title: Concessions for Peace
subtitle: Could any treasure on earth possibly fill the void our losses have left?

items.text: Concessions for Peace

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: *sigh*
The bored and idle remnant of Squad "XII" carries out her as yet tedious orders.
She stops by a window, squinting inside.
Broken furniture and cobwebs woven between cracked and forgotten china.
A uniquely shaped counter-arcanum monitoring device disrupts the decaying scene.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Clearly no one's bothered to do any cleanup, then.
She opens the window and leans in, her mask blocking out the sudden puff of dust.
Following her officer's instructions, she pulls out a transparent strip of cloth and places it by the device.
The cloth changes color rapidly, and a line of neat letters appears on its surface.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: "Counter-arcanum device operating normally." Looks like I'm not needed here either.
She climbs back out the window.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Hmph. Hmm? Aren't you ...?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Merel.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Marsha?
The young soldier springs up to greet her, visibly relieved.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: It really is you! You're back finally!

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Is Paravyan alright?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Oh, poor guy's had a hard time of it, but at least he's still in one piece. He's lying in a sickbed as we speak. He should recover soon.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: It's too bad he didn't find anything too useful in the village, well, aside from that armored vehicle.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Fortunately, Sentinel happened to be there at the same time.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: So it really was her, the one who assassinated Colonel Hirschfelder?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Yes. She'd collected a wealth of evidence concerning Manus Vindictae. I've already delivered it to Commander Creius.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: As for the assassination, it turns out her actions weren't entirely unjustifiable. Let's just consider it a misunderstanding.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Misunderstanding? She literally killed a guy.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: She's not the only one.
Marsha unconsciously rubs the old scars on her palms, feeling them itch like never before.
Merel presses her lips together, creating a twisted crease in her mask.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Well, I ... Anyway, I was just worried that something bad might've happened to you, like what happened to ...

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: To whom?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Charles and Amanda. We haven't heard from them in over four hours now.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: They were dispatched to investigate Hill 299, correct? Has any help been sent their way?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Commander Creius sent some men to look for them. Hopefully, we'll hear some good news soon.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Most of the other teams have finished their investigations. A few of them are already in the safe zone, actually. Apparently, they've found a lot of useful info.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: So, we won't have to head back out again, right?
Merel watches Marsha carefully, as if waiting for her to confirm something.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: The front's getting shelled to hell and back. I mean, chances are we'll ...
Marsha pats her on the shoulder.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: The evidence Sentinel provided is quite damning. Our job here will be over just as soon as we can get ahold of the team at Hill 299.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Don't worry.
Copies of the evidence Marsha submitted have been spread across the table.
Personal letters, marked military maps, battle plans, engineering blueprints, defaced and altered documents ...
Along with them on the table are exhibits recovered by other investigators from across the front line, arranged in rough chronological order starting from 1918.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: This is unbelievable!
He stares at the pile, the sheer flood of information overwhelming him.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: These documents ... The evidence is undeniable. Every one of those absurd conspiracy theories was true. The 1918 peace negotiations really were sabotaged by Manus Vindictae!

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: The nations on both sides of this war have been under the deception of an invisible enemy. It is no wonder that even the victors of the 1919 offensive gained no real advantage.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: My God. To think Manus Vindictae has been sharing war secrets with both sides to ensure neither can win this war.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: That they have used our commanders as tools for their massacre. It is nigh on unimaginable!
He looks up with sudden realization.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: This does not simply concern one nation. These documents could topple nearly all of Europe's military leaders.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: With this list of Manus defectors in our hands, and if we act with haste, we may finally put every one of them behind bars.
Waiting for Georg's mood to stabilize, Creius adds a word of advice.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Let me remind you that Laplace may be able to heal these so-called "defectors." Eberhard's case proved that the Manus's mental influence can be purged.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: Yes, yes, of course. Whatever the case, we must act as soon as possible. The chancellor and the parliament are prepared to strike.
Finding light in a once grim future, he starts to shake, sending ripples through the papers in his hands.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Agreed. The evidence is sufficient. There is no need to delay.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: Wonderful! Just think of the soldiers finally making their way home.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: This is the day we secure a century of peace for Europe!

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Hmph. Sounds like a line for the history books.
He has no mind to react to Creius's parting jab. Stuffing all the documents into his briefcase, he rushes out.
Straightening the remaining mess on his desk, Creius retrieves a hidden communicator.
It's been connected the entire time.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Everything's going according to plan.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Good. The other teams have shared the same intelligence with the pacifist political leaders in their respective regions.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: All the Foundation has to do now is watch for any interference from Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But, won't this approach cause even more turbulence?

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Timekeeper?
He had been expecting the faction leaders, making this an unexpected relief.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Oh, yes, Creius. I was just listening in.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: I see. In any case, the outcome can't be worse than the war we're living through, Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: As I'm sure you learned in your history studies, this war claimed tens of millions of soldiers' lives.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Not to mention the equally massive number of civilian casualties, whether direct or otherwise.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: We are now two years on from what should've been the end of this war. The death toll has already climbed much higher, and it will only continue to rise if we don't put an end to it soon.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: At least our efforts have won us a marginally better outcome.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I see.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: In short, the war is already over.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Once the pacifist political parties take power, an armistice will surely be signed in Montpaix.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: This may not be the time, but I have a question to ask.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Does the Foundation Committee have any contingency plans should things take a turn for the worse?
The silence in the room confirms the suspicions of the voice on the other end.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Did you notice something suspicious?
The former vigil officer fishes out as many suspicious details from his memories as he can.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: It's about Hirschfelder's assassination ...

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Do you remember a certain detail from Marsha's report?

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: You think his death to be the spark of a reignited war, but, even if I had stayed my hand from him, your plans would have been for naught.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: If that were so, why would the Manus risk exposing Hirschfelder? Why would they allow him to meet with the Foundation in Montpaix?

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: If Hirschfelder hadn't been killed, would the negotiations have become a fruitless tug-of-war?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Manus Vindictae would only cooperate with the Foundation on something that was sure to fail.
An intuitive guess is assembled, drawing on the experience of prior contact with Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Could it be that they're purposely diverting our attention?

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: My thoughts exactly, Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: That said, securing peace is our top priority at the moment.
